[BBC Business] US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn
Shares in Intel continue to fall while the tech-heavy Nasdaq opens at its lowest level in more than two months.

[BBC Business] What we know about Binance's $6.3bn hack
Cyber correspondent Joe Tidy explains more about what is suspected to be the biggest hack in history.

[BBC Business] City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist
Ian Thomas, who heads the City of London Corporation, tops the Black Powerlist in its 21st year.

[BBC Business] From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes
A new generation is embracing eye-catching patching and visible mends.

[CNBC] Treasury Department announces new Series I bond rate of 5.51% for the next six months
The U.S. Department of the Treasury has announced new Series I bond rates through April 2027.

[CNBC] Binance hack: Investigators in a 'cat and mouse game' to recover $6.3 billion in stolen funds
More than $6 billion in crypto was stolen from Binance, setting off a race to recover the funds before North Korea-linked hackers can launder them into cash.

[CNBC] 'Bad time to troll': Binance cofounder Changpeng Zhao asks Elon Musk for 'respect' after post about bitcoin hack
Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao asked Elon Musk to stop “trolling” after a $6.3 billion hack, pointing to Binance’s $1 billion-plus SpaceX stake.

[CNBC] Why bitcoin held up better after the record Binance hack
Bitcoin was trading down about 4% on Friday afternoon, less than a day after the biggest crypto hack in history.

[MarketWatch] Microsoft is winning the cloud wars and becoming Wall Street’s new golden child
Various factors indicate that Microsoft is in a better financial position than its cloud rivals, analysts say.

[MarketWatch] ‘He was heartbroken’: My husband’s kids abandoned him when he was dying. Was he right to leave everything to me?
“In the end, he left them a few sentimental mementos, some collectibles and old photographs.”

[MarketWatch] American workers are finding their take-home pay isn’t keeping up with inflation, with their wallets ‘stretched thinner and thinner’
Worker compensation grows slower than inflation for second straight quarter

[MarketWatch] You can expect the stock market to rally no matter who wins on Election Day
Also in Weekend Reads: Dividend stocks, a way to jump on the Anthropic bandwagon ahead of its IPO, and advice from The Moneyist.
